solution.body:
[IMG]


Let's consider $T$ tension in string and a acceleration of blocks.

FBD of $4\mathrm{kg}$


[IMG]


$4g\sin θ-\mathrm{T}=4\mathrm{a}$ 

$\frac{4g\sqrt{3}}{2}-T=4a$ .........(1)

FBD of $1\mathrm{kg}$


[IMG]


$T-g\sin 30^{\circ }=a$

$T-\frac{g}{2}=a...(2)$

From (1) and (2), we get

$\frac{4g\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{g}{2}=5a$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{g\left (4\sqrt{3}-1\right )}{2}=5a$

$\Rightarrow$ $5a=\frac{10\left (4\sqrt{3}-1\right )}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a=\left (4\sqrt{3}-1\right )$ $m/s^{2}$

By putting value of "a" in equation (2), we get

$T-\frac{10}{2}=\left (4\sqrt{3}-1\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $T=\left (4\sqrt{3}-1\right )+5$ = $\left (4\sqrt{3}+4\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $T=4(\sqrt{3}+1)N$

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : If the Brewster's angle for the light propagating from air to glass is $θ_{\mathrm{B}}$, then the Brewster's angle for the light propagating from glass to air is $\frac{π}{2}-θ_{B}$

Statement II : The Brewster's angle for the light propagating from glass to air is $\tan ^{-1}(μ_{\mathrm{g}})$ where $μ_{\mathrm{g}}$ is the refractive index of glass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At the Brewster angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, so the angle of incidence $i_{B}$ and the angle of refraction $r$ satisfy $i_{B}+r=90^{\circ }$, i.e. $\sin r=\cos i_{B}$.

Air to glass: Snell's law gives $\sin θ_{B}=μ_{g}\sin r=μ_{g}\cos θ_{B}$, so

$\tan θ_{B}=μ_{g}\Rightarrow θ_{B}=\tan ^{-1}(μ_{g})$

Glass to air: Snell's law gives $μ_{g}\sin θ_{B}^{'}=\sin r^{'}=\cos θ_{B}^{'}$, so

$\tan θ_{B}^{'}=\dfrac{1}{μ_{g}}=\dfrac{1}{\tan θ_{B}}=\tan \left (\dfrac{π}{2}-θ_{B}\right )\Rightarrow θ_{B}^{'}=\dfrac{π}{2}-θ_{B}$

Hence Statement I is true.

Statement II gives $\tan ^{-1}(μ_{g})$, which is the Brewster angle for light going from air to glass; for glass to air it is $\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{μ_{g}}\right )$ (for $μ_{g}=1.5$, about $33.7^{\circ }$ rather than $56.3^{\circ }$). Hence Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: The weight of a body at the surface of earth is 18 N. The weight of the body at an altitude of 3200 km above the earth's surface is (given, radius of earth $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}=6400\mathrm{km}$) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The weight of an object at a height h from the Earth's surface is given by:

$W^{'}=W\left (\frac{R}{R+h}\right )^{2}$

where:

W' is the weight at height h,
W is the weight at the Earth's surface,
R is the radius of the Earth,
h is the height above the Earth's surface.

In this problem, the weight at the Earth's surface W is given as 18 N, the radius of the Earth R is given as 6400 km, and the height h is given as 3200 km. Substituting these values into the equation gives:

$W^{'}=18N\left (\frac{6400km}{6400km+3200km}\right )^{2}=18N\left (\frac{2}{3}\right )^{2}=18N\cdot \frac{4}{9}=8N$

Therefore, the weight of the body at an altitude of 3200 km above the Earth's surface is 8 N.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

B. The saturation current increases as the intensity of incident light increases.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) From Einstein's equation

$K_{\max }=eV_{s}=hv-𝜙$

Form the stopping potential $(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}})$ depends on $𝜙$ $&v$.

(B) Saturation current is proportional to intensity, i.e., number of incident photons.

(C) $K_{\max }$ only depends on nature of photon and $𝜙$.

(D) Einstein used particle behaviour of photon to explain photon electric effect.

Only B is correct.

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : An elevator can go up or down with uniform speed when its weight is balanced with the tension of its cable.

Statement II : Force exerted by the floor of an elevator on the foot of a person standing on it  is more than his/her weight when the elevator goes down with increasing speed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: when the cable tension equals the weight of the elevator, the net force on it is zero, so its acceleration is zero and it can move up or down with uniform speed. Statement I is true.

Statement II: an elevator going down with increasing speed has a downward acceleration $a$. For the person standing on the floor,

$mg-N=ma\Rightarrow N=m(g-a)<mg$

The floor pushes on the feet with a force less than the weight, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text: A hollow cylindrical conductor has length of 3.14 m, while its inner and outer diameters are 4 mm and 8 mm respectively. The resistance of the conductor is $n\times 10^{-3}\Omega$. If the resistivity of the material is $2.4\times 10^{-8}\Omega \mathrm{m}$, the value of $n$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Resistance of the hollow cylindrical conductor is given by, 

$R=ρ\frac{l}{π\left (r_{2}^{2}-r_{1}^{2}\right )}$

where $r_{2}=$ outer radius

$\begin{array}{l} r_{1}=\text{inner radius} \\  \\ ρ=\text{resistivity,}l=\text{length} \\  \\ \therefore R=\dfrac{2.4\times 10^{-8}\times 3.14}{π\left (\frac{8^{2}}{4}-\frac{4^{2}}{4}\right )\times 10^{-6}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{2.4\times 10^{-8}\times 4}{48\times 10^{-6}}=2\times 10^{-3}\Omega  \end{array}$

text: Vectors $a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ and $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}$ are perpendicular to each other when $3a+2b=7$, the ratio of $a$ to $b$ is $\frac{x}{2}$. The value of $x$ is $____________$.

text:
As shown in the figure, a combination of a thin plano concave lens and a thin plano convex lens is used to image an object placed at infinity. The radius of curvature of both the lenses is 30 cm and refraction index of the material for both the lenses is 1.75. Both the lenses are placed at distance of 40 cm from each other. Due to the combination, the image of the object is formed at distance $x=$ $_________ cm$, from concave lens.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{1}{f_{\text{concave}}}=(1.75-1)\left (\frac{1}{\infty }-\frac{1}{+30}\right )=-\frac{0.75}{30}$

$f_{\text{concave}}=-40\mathrm{cm}$

$\frac{1}{f_{\text{convex}}}=(1.75-1)\left (\frac{1}{30}-\frac{1}{\infty }\right )=\frac{0.75}{30}$

$f_{\text{convex}}=40\mathrm{cm}$

Let the first image is formed at $v_{1}$ so

$\frac{1}{v_{1}}-\frac{1}{\infty }=\frac{1}{f_{\text{concave}}}=-\frac{1}{40}$

$\Rightarrow v_{1}=-40\mathrm{cm}$

for second image

$\frac{1}{x-40}-\frac{1}{-80}=\frac{1}{40}$

$\Rightarrow x=120\mathrm{cm}$

text: A stream of positively charged particles having $\frac{q}{m}=2\times 10^{11}\frac{C}{kg}$ and velocity $\vec{v}_{0}=3\times 10^{7}\hat{i}m/s$ is deflected by an electric field $1.8\hat{j}$ kV/m. The electric field exists in a region of 10 cm along $x$ direction. Due to the electric field, the deflection of the charged particles in the $y$ direction is $_________ mm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} a_{y}=\dfrac{qE_{y}}{m} \\  \\ a_{y}=2\times 10^{11}\times 1800 \\  \\ =36\times 10^{13}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2} \\  \\ \text{Time}=\dfrac{10\times 10^{-2}}{v_{0}}=\dfrac{0.1}{3\times 10^{7}}=\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\times 10^{-8}\right )\sec \text{.} \\  \\ \therefore \quad y=\dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 36\times 10^{13}\times \left (\dfrac{1}{3}\times 10^{-8}\right )^{2} \\  \\ =2\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m} \\  \\ =2\mathrm{mm} \\  \end{array}$

text: A spherical body of mass 2 kg starting from rest acquires a kinetic energy of 10000 J at the end of $5^{\mathrm{th}}$ second. The force acted on the body is $________ N$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the force be $F$ so acceleration $a=\frac{F}{m}$

So displacement $S=\frac{1}{2}at^{2}=\frac{Ft^{2}}{2m}$

So work done $W=F.S=\frac{F^{2}t^{2}}{2m}$

From work energy Theorem

$\Delta KE=W$

$W=\frac{F^{2}t^{2}}{2m}=10000$

$F=\sqrt{\frac{10000\times 2\times 2}{5^{2}}}$

$F=40\mathrm{N}$
